thread:
maria: Heads up — ran a focused perf pass this morning on the AWQ weight-only path with our new batching scheduler heuristics. Seeing a reproducible tail latency bump (~10–14%) on KV-cache-heavy chat sessions when group_size=32 and packing enabled.
ajay: ouch. can you share the profile? is it CPU or GPU bound?
maria: Attached top-line: GPU kernels look fine, but a bunch of small memcpy/serial unpack ops spike on the CPU side right before kernel launch. stacktrace from perfbot below.
perfbot: automated profile (snippet):
```
SAMPLING: 10s
CPU  62%  memcpy
CPU  18%  pack_unwind()
CPU  10%  kv_eviction_check()
CUDA 95% kernels happy
```
linh: that sounds like packing/unpacking starvation — might be prefetch not keeping up for the new scheduler that groups many short prefixes together. scheduler now coalesces small requests into a single batch more aggressively, right?
maria: correct. new scheduler merges <16-token prefixes across endpoints to hit GPU throughput targets. Problem is we sometimes pack mixed group sizes (32/64) from different requests; the packer serializes per-tensor copying.
azay: (note: ajay is on PTO, but chiming in) can we avoid serial tensor copies by using an iovec-style gather or pinned staging buffer?
ajay: idea: allocate a per-worker pinned slab and do threaded scatter so memcpy happens in parallel. but need to measure contention on kmalloc/pinned pages.
linh: related: with AWQ group_size=32 we save compute but increase number of micro-batches; that increases pack/unpack ops. GPu kernel time goes down but CPU pre/post work rises.
zach: any quality regressions with AWQ @ gsize 32 vs 64 we should track. Did calibration change?
maria: we used the same calibration dataset; no perplexity shift >0.5% across eval set. This is perf-only.
ajay: curious if GPTQ path behaves differently — fewer unpack ops because we pack differently? anyone tested GPTQ in identical scheduler config?
linh: I ran a short A/B — GPTQ group_size=32 had slightly less CPU unpack overhead, possibly because our GPTQ serializer writes contiguous pages once per group, unlike AWQ's per-channel packing that interleaves.
maria: TLDR: AWQ + aggressive coalescing -> CPU packing hotspots. Root cause: per-request packing loop is single-threaded and uses non-pinned buffers.
perfbot: repro command (internal):
```
./perf_client --model rdlw-awq-v2 --group-size 32 --scheduler coalesce --threads 8 --kv-heavy
# run 2000 sessions
```
maria: quick mitigation I prototyped: enable "staged_pinned_pool" for packer + allow parallel memcpy across 4 worker threads. Did a sanity run: tail latency drop back to baseline, throughput unaffected.
ajay: nice. any memory/regressions? pinned pool increases resident memory by ~12% in the test. ok tradeoff?
maria: we need an opt-in config per deployment tier. For Dedicated customers we can enable by default; hosted could be opt-out.
zach: we should also add telemetry: counters for pack_bytes, pack_ops, parallel_copy_failures, pinned_pool_allocs. then we can emit per-route counters and detect when packing dominates CPU.
linh: agree. add a per-model flag that switches serializer layout to GPTQ-like contiguous output for AWQ as a fallback. cheaper to implement and may avoid pinned pools in some cases.
ajay: long-term: kernel-side solution — add a kernel that accepts a scatter/gather list so we avoid CPU copy entirely. but that needs CUDA-level changes and driver pinned registration.
maria: filing two action items: 1) short-term: staged_pinned_pool + threaded memcpy + feature flag (maria -> PR), 2) medium-term: serializer layout fallback (linh -> spike), 3) long-term: native SG CUDA kernel exploration (zach -> design doc).
perfbot: ticket created: PERF-2421 (AWQ pack hotspots)
maria: I'll post microbench numbers to the PR: pre: median 45ms / p99 132ms; post prototype: median 43ms / p99 116ms (kv-heavy chat). Will run 24h soak.
ajay: thanks. also capture kernel selection telemetry — which kernel variant got chosen for each batch, sequence length distribution, and quantized bitwidth used. helps root-cause whether kernel choice amplified packing overhead.
maria: noted. I'll add per-batch kernel_id, group_size, pack_time, unpack_time to telemetry.
zach: thanks team. good triage. emoji :thumbsup:
